rounds.fact: The famously sparse homepage was reportedly a side effect of the founders not knowing HTML well enough to make anything more complex. An early advantage the world mistook for minimalist genius.
EarthLink grew into one of the largest ISPs of the dial-up era by positioning itself as friendlier and more customer-focused than AOL, its biggest rival.
Vimeo launched in 2004 and deliberately positioned itself as the artsier, higher-quality alternative to YouTube, banning gaming and vlog content in its early years to keep that focus.
Match.com launched in 1995 and is one of the very first online dating sites, predating the smartphone-app dating era by almost two decades.
Foursquare's whole early identity was built around competitive check-ins and 'mayorships' of physical locations, a gamified feature that mostly disappeared as the app pivoted toward recommendations.
